title: The Art of Theatre
description: Introduction to theatre as a reflection of society and a contributor to the world of art. Students explore theatre’s continuing relevance to contemporary culture. Attendance at selected theatre events required.

title: Voice and Movement
description: Project-based preparation of physical and vocal instrument for acting.
notes: Not open to students with credit in Theatre 110.

title: Acting for Nonmajors
description: Improvisational exercises (verbal and nonverbal) in sensory awareness, observation, concentration, listening, and response skills with application to other fields. Individual presentation techniques for the preprofessional in other disciplines.

title: Heritage of Storytelling
description: Survey of significant concepts over a wide history of theatre, television, and film. Analysis of classical, contemporary, realistic, and avant-garde examples; exploring influence of historical narrative forms on contemporary storytelling.

title: Acting I
description: Development of individual’s ability to express thought and emotion through effective use of the voice and body. These fundamental concepts may be applied to stage, film, and television acting.

title: American Musical on Stage and Screen
description: Shows, films, and performers that trace the evolution of this unique American art form from its origins to contemporary Broadway, film, and pop culture, utilizing live performance and digital media.

title: Asian-American Theatre & Performances
description: Introduces Asian American theatre, beginning in the 1970s with political roots. Through dramatic works and critical studies, it explores Asian American narratives, cultural interventions, and the multiplicity of identities-race, gender, class-revealed in the theatre, highlighting how different waves of immigration and generations express themselves theatrically.

title: Acting II
description: Continuation of

title: Theatre Design and Technology I
description: Design, technical practices, and production organization for the theatre.

title: Experimental Topics
description: Selected topics.
notes: See Class Schedule for specific content. Limit of nine units of any combination of 296, 496, 596 courses applicable to a bachelor’s degree.

title: Special Study
description: Individual study.

title: Chicano/a Performance: Introduction to Latina/o Cultural Production on Stage and Screen
description: Explores contemporary representations of Latinas/os in media, examining how performance reflects gender, class, race, sexuality, and nationality. Students will analyze visual strategies and apply civic engagement theories, fostering a comprehensive understanding of Latinas/os on stage and screen.

title: Creative Drama I
description: Current philosophies, principles, and techniques of creative drama. Development of the individual through use of dramatic play, imagination, improvisation, and theatre games. Applicable to classroom teaching, counseling, recreation, and senior citizen programs.

title: Theatre for Young Audiences
description: Current philosophies and practices in theatre for young audiences. Techniques of selecting and producing plays for and with youth. Theatre styles, script analysis, and functions of the production team.

title: Advanced Voice and Text for Actors: Select Heightened Speech From the Greeks to Today
description: Techniques of vocal expression in the theatre, primarily in plays with heightened and elevated speech, e.g. Shakespeare and classic Greek drama.

title: Script Analysis
description: Analysis of representative plays with emphasis on plot and character development, dramatic structure, action, and style.

title: Individual Vocal Instruction
description: Individual voice instruction/coaching for students in B.A. Musical Theatre degree program

title: Acting III
description: Continuation of

title: Stage Management-Theory
description: Development of the prompt script, organizational methods, and collaborative personnel interaction.

title: Stage Management-Practicum
description: Practical experience in stage managing department productions.

title: Theatre Marketing and Publicity
description: Practical experience in marketing and publicity for theatres, including PSAs, press releases, layout-graphics for written materials, magazine and newspaper advertisements, marketing strategy and campaign development for a full theatre season.

title: Theatrical Makeup
description: Planning and application of makeup for stage, film, and television. Classroom exercises and production-related activities.

title: Musical Theatre Performance I
description: Basic performance techniques in musical theatre. Application of acting theory to musical theatre literature.

title: Musical Theatre Performance II
description: Basic performance techniques in musical theatre. Vocal/performance style and vocal production related to period/style musical theatre literature, solo/group/audition presentation.

title: Musical Theatre Dance
description: Musical theatre dance techniques to include classic jazz and ballet. Movement vocabulary and choreographic styles utilized in musical theatre production.

title: Movement for the Theatre I
description: Activities to develop physical skills of the performer. Links between imagination, movement, and body expression leading to character development.

title: Directing I
description: Principles and techniques of directing for the stage: play selection, analysis, and interpretation; casting methods; stage composition and movement; and rehearsal procedures.

title: African American Theatre and Performance
description: An exploration into the historical, political, and social struggles that have inspired the creation of African American Theatre, Television, and Film. Students will be encouraged to seek, develop and express their own creative voices.

title: Workshop in Improvisational Acting
description: Theories and principles of improvisational acting.

title: Audition and Business Skills for the Actor
description: Auditioning and interviewing for stage and screen; selecting audition pieces, rehearsing, performing auditions. Business skills of audition process; researching individual marketability, branding, networking to secure auditions and representation.

title: Acting on Camera
description: Director-actor-camera collaborations in rehearsal and performance, using single or multi camera television technique. Techniques for preparing and performing monologues and scenes with practical experience in front of and behind the camera.

title: Shakespeare Touring Production
description: Participate in high school outreach touring production.

title: Scene Design I
description: Techniques and procedures in application of design, color, and perspective in designing scenery.

title: Practicum in Theatrical Production: Scenery Construction
description: Technical theatre production experience for departmental public performances.

title: Practicum in Theatrical Production: Costume Construction
description: Technical theatre production experience for departmental public performances.

title: Practicum in Theatrical Production: Lighting
description: Technical theatre production experience for departmental public performances. C. Stage Lighting.

title: Practicum in Performance: Stage Crew
description: Practical experience working as a crew member on one of three departmental productions. Arranged activity, schedules distributed in class. Most activities take place during evening and weekend hours. Average 70 hours per semester.

title: Practicum in Performance: Costume Crew
description: Practical experience working as a costume crew member on one of three departmental productions. Arranged activity, schedules distributed in class. Most activities take place during evening and weekend hours. Average 70 hours per semester.

title: Practicum in Performance: Cast Member
description: Practical experience in departmental public performances.

title: Practicum in Performance: Lighting Crew
description: Practical experience working as a lighting crew member on one of three departmental productions. Arranged activity, schedules distributed in class. Most activities take place during evening and weekend hours. Average 70 hours per semester.

title: Lighting Design I
description: Concepts and technologies in lighting for theatre and related performance areas. Emphasis on mechanics of stage lighting, color, instruments, and control. Laboratory and production related activities.

title: Portfolio Preparation and Exit Interview
description: Transition to the industry of design and technology for theatre, television, and film by examining the self-marketing materials required to enter the workforce after graduation. Culmination in exit interview.

title: Musical Theatre Performance III
description: Advanced rehearsal/performance techniques in musical theatre. Performance style, vocal production, and staging relating to musical theatre literature: duet and small group presentation.

title: Musical Theatre Performance IV
description: Advanced rehearsal/performance techniques in musical theatre. Collaboration, performance preparation, acting/singing styles, vocal production, and staging that result in a final performance for an audience.

title: Costume Design I
description: Theory and creative application of principles of costume design for various types of production. Emphasis on concept development, character interpretation, research methods, color organization, and fabric selection. Laboratory and production related activities.

title: Directing II
description: Experience and group evaluation in directing one-act plays before an audience. Attendance at selected public performances required.

title: History of the Theatre
description: Theatre from ancient times to the present. Special attention given to the theatre as a mirror of the social and cultural background of various countries and periods in which it is studied.

title: History of the Theatre
description: Theatre from ancient times to the present. Special attention given to the theatre as a mirror of the social and cultural background of various countries and periods in which it is studied.

title: Theatre of Diversity
description: Racial, ethnic, political, and social diversity of American landscape as reflected in works of major playwrights of diversity.

title: Facility Operations and Management for Theatre
description: Leadership, managing creative teams, budgeting, scheduling, liability and safety, co-producing, special event and corporate entertainment production management. Front of house operations to include house management, box office operations, ticketing, budgeting and reporting.

title: Event Coordination and the Entertainment Industry
description: All aspects of producing special events, including venue designs and planning, managerial roles of entertainment industry, and how venue planning affects business decisions of these various managers.

title: Theatre Internship
description: Work with approved theatre organizations off-campus under the combined supervision of theatre personnel and instructors.

title: Experimental Topics
description: Selected topics.
notes: See Class Schedule for specific content. Limit of nine units of any combination of 296, 496, 596 courses applicable to a bachelor’s degree.

title: Special Study
description: Individual study.

title: Creative Drama and Language Arts
description: Advanced techniques in using creative drama to teach literature and language. Emphasis on use of drama in teaching of reading and world literature. Practical experience through fieldwork in elementary or middle school classrooms.

title: Playwriting
description: Writing for the stage and public presentation. Characterization, dialogue, and formal experimentation when writing short plays.

title: Dramaturgy
description: Theory and application of various aspects of dramaturgy and theatre literary management. Production-oriented synthesis of advanced text analysis, dramatic theory and criticism, historical research, and dramatic literature. Attendance at select plays required.

title: Period Dress and Decor: Ancient World Through Eighteenth Century
description: Visual survey of relationships and cultural significance of period dress, architecture, and decorative arts as applied to theatrical productions. Emphasis on significant historic periods in dramatic literature.
notes: Theatre 530A is not open to students with credit in Theatre 530.

title: Period Dress and Decor: NeoClassical Through Twentieth Century
description: Visual survey of relationships and cultural significance of period dress, architecture, and decorative arts as applied to theatrical productions. Emphasis on significant historic periods in dramatic literature.

title: Advanced Topics in Stage and Screen Performance
description: Theory and practice in performance from theatre, television, and film to include physical theatre, voice and speech, film and theatre performance styles, intercultural theatre, devised work.

title: Theory and Styles in Acting and Directing
description: Acting and directing challenges in theory and style related to the production of plays from great periods in theatre history, with attention to characterization, creative directing, dramatic values, and production approaches.

title: Wig Construction and Period Hair Styling
description: Wig construction and period hairstyling for the entertainment industry. History of hairstyles and the social function of follicle aesthetics of various cultures from antiquity through the twenty-first century.

title: Production and Event Management in the Arts
description: Advanced theory and practice of professional event management and production in the visual and performing arts.

title: Theatre Rendering
description: Rendering for scenic, costume, and lighting designers. Techniques, media, and portfolio preparation.

title: Scene Design II
description: History of scene design and application of contemporary styles to various types of dramatic productions.

title: Scene Painting
description: Theories and techniques of scene painting, including both historical backgrounds and modern procedures. Full-scale projects executed in scenery studio.

title: Studio Skills for Theatre: Model Making
description: Traditional model-making for scenic designers. Media, presentation, and techniques of work.

title: Advanced Stage Technologies
description: Design and fabrication of stage machinery and special effects. Computer-based automation and controls, electro-mechanical systems, and programmable logic controllers. Current U.S. and European machinery standards and safety systems.

title: Mechanical Drawing for the Theatre
description: Theatre drafting standards and techniques. Floor plans, sections, elevations, perspective drawings, and light plots.

title: CADD for the Theatre
description: Computer aided drafting applications for theatre designers.

title: Lighting Design II
description: Advanced design theories and lighting practice for the entertainment arts.
notes: Recommended co-requisite THEA 556: Digital Communication for Lighting Design. Plus fee.

title: Sound Design for the Theatre
description: Theories and techniques of sound design and reinforcement for theatrical performance. Laboratory experience in sound production.

title: Lighting and Sound Technology
description: Use of electrics for the stage. Lighting, sound, computer. Practical applications emphasized.

title: Software for Theatrical Design
description: Application of computer software for theatre, including scenery, costume, lighting, and sound design.

title: Advanced Media Design
description: Digital media creation for theatrical use. Creation of video content for projection design and integrated media. Advanced digital painting of theatrical renderings.

title: Costume Design II
description: Advanced studies in costume design. Emphasis on theatrical style, rendering layout, design problems, materials, and budget.

title: Technical Direction
description: Modern technical direction including project management (budgeting and procurement, managing employees); design and engineering; automation, rigging, advanced stagecraft (metalcraft, CNC machinery, composite construction), and safety.

title: Costume Design Technology I
description: Current materials and practices of costume technology: advanced construction techniques, fabric selection and use, period pattern drafting, draping, and cutting.

title: Costume Design Technology II
description: Advanced costume craft construction techniques and management procedures for costume production: millinery, fabric dyeing and painting, jewelry, and related crafts.

title: Movement for the Theatre II
description: Musical theatre movement and dance styles.

title: Digital Communication for Lighting Design
description: Application of Lightwright, Vectorworks, and other industry-standard software programs to produce 2D/3D light plots, 3D lighting renderings, and professional quality lighting design package documentation. Communication techniques, drawing organization, and industry practices.

title: 3D Fabrication for Entertainment Design
description: Theory and practice of basic principles of 3D printing and scanning for theatrical use. Basics of fused deposition modeling manufacture. Sourcing and creating 3D models. Creation and realization of original work.

title: Welding and Metal Fabrication for Theatre
description: This course covers the fundamentals of welding and fabrication techniques for the construction of theatrical scenery.

title: Programming for Live Events
description: In-depth, hands-on experience programming lighting consoles for a diverse range of live events. Emphasis on moving, multi-attribute fixtures, and effects.

title: Projection Design and Integrated Media
description: Designing projections and integrated media for theatrical productions.

title: Costume Topics
description: Fashion for costume design, Hollywood costume design in the past century, origins of modern menswear, psychology and meaning of dress.

title: Practicum in Theatrical Production: Independent Study
description: Design projects in areas of scenery, costume, lighting, sound, or makeup.

title: Practicum in Theatrical Production: Design for Department Public Performances
description: Design projects in areas of scenery, costume, lighting, sound, or makeup.

title: Theatre and Racial Protests: The Civil Rights to the Apartheid Movements
description: Explores the intersection of performance and activism during the American Civil Rights Movement and South African anti-Apartheid struggle. Students analyze protest theatre’s role in articulating resistance, influencing change, and promoting racial justice, studying key productions, historical contexts, and performative strategies from the Negro Ensemble, National Black Theatre, and Market Theatre. Students registered at the 500 level will be expected to expand beyond the treatments and synopsis, into the creation of individual short scripts.

title: Theatre in the Classroom
description: Methods of teaching theatre in elementary, middle, and secondary schools. Emphasis on pedagogy, organization of curriculum, play selection, and principles of producing plays in the classroom.

title: Selected Topics in Theatre
description: A specialized study of selected topics from the areas of theatre.

title: Writing for Theatre
description: Advanced study of forms and methods of writing to include critical writing for theatre. Making appropriate rhetorical choices for different writing contexts and the uses of research in writing.

title: Seminar in Design Aesthetics for Theatre, Television, and Film
description: Aesthetic theories and practice. Design aesthetics as applied to theatre, television, film and new media production.

title: Seminar in History of Musical Theatre: Nineteenth Century Viennese Operetta through 1950
description: Chronological survey of representative works from musical theatre history including major productions, personalities, styles, and genres.

title: Seminar in History of Musical Theatre: 1950 to present
description: Chronological survey of representative works from musical theatre history including major productions, personalities, styles, and genres.

title: Seminar in Theories of the Theatre
description: Theories of dramatic literature and performance, reflecting major stylistic movements and aesthetic philosophies of the stage from the classical Greeks to today (e.g., Aristotle, Lessing, Appia, Brecht, and Grotowski).

title: History of Musical Theatre Laboratory
description: Laboratory component of

title: History of Musical Theatre Laboratory
description: Laboratory component of

title: Seminar in Musical Theatre Script and Score Analysis
description: Representative works from musical theatre analyzed in terms of dramatic and musical aesthetics.

title: Musical Theatre Studio
description: Acting, singing, and movement skills in relation to musical theatre performance.
